new_entities.name: Semaglutide for obesity-related HFpEF
aliases: GLP-1 receptor agonism for obesity-related HFpEF
new_entities.description: Use of semaglutide in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity, with or without type 2 diabetes.

new_entities.name: Clinical outcomes
new_entities.description: Clinical outcomes such as symptoms, functional capacity, heart-failure events, and other patient-centered trial outcomes.

edges.effect_quant: STEP-HFpEF improved KCCQ-CSS by 7.8 points versus placebo and increased 6-minute walk distance by 20.3 m. STEP-HFpEF DM showed similar symptom and functional gains in patients with diabetes, and HFpEF-focused GLP-1 meta-analysis found fewer heart-failure events overall (RR 0.40) with clear improvements in KCCQ-CSS and walking distance.
edges.population: adults with obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, including both non-diabetic and type 2 diabetic subgroups
edges.mechanism: Semaglutide likely improves obesity-related HFpEF through weight loss, reduced inflammatory burden, improved exercise tolerance, and favorable hemodynamic unloading.
edges.summary: The semaglutide HFpEF-obesity story is strong for symptoms and functional capacity, and it now has supportive pooled evidence for fewer heart-failure events. This is one of the clearest examples of phenotype-targeted therapy in HFpEF.
edges.caveats: The most mature evidence is on symptoms, quality of life, and exercise capacity rather than hard mortality endpoints. Generalization beyond obesity-related HFpEF should be cautious.

evidence.citation: Kosiborod MN et al 2023 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Semaglutide in Patients with Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Obesity. STEP-HFpEF.

effect_quant.comparator: KCCQ-CSS change at 52 weeks with semaglutide versus placebo in STEP-HFpEF
